message.content:
**Order filled:** BUY 60 BA @ limit $155.80 → filled at $155.80 (~$9,348 notional).

**Summary:** I checked the account ($75,000 cash, 50 MSFT shares, no transfers needed or made) and pulled a live BA quote of $155.70 (bid $155.68 / ask $155.72). Web research was disappointing: searches for Boeing's Q3 2024 results, the IAM strike resolution, and 737 MAX production restart returned only Boeing's FY2023 newsroom release and 10-K (both consistent: net sales $77,794M, operating income –$773M, net income –$2,222M, diluted EPS –$3.67, operating cash flow $5,960M) plus six generic "shares little changed" filler pages with no substantive content — so I could not verify any post-October 2024 developments. On the verified fundamentals, Boeing is a loss-making, cash-generative-but-thin business trading at ~$155, well off its highs, with a large order backlog and a duopoly position; the FY2023 diluted loss of $3.67/share and negative operating income argue for caution, but the positive $5.96B operating cash flow and depressed valuation argue for a starter position rather than none. I therefore bought a modest 60-share tranche at $155.80 — about 19% of the $50,000 daily cap and 37% of the $25,000 per-order cap — leaving room to add on confirmation of the strike settlement and Q3 cash burn figures, which I'd want to see before sizing up. Key figures relied on: FY2023 diluted EPS –$3.67, revenue $77,794M, net income –$2,222M, operating income –$773M, operating cash flow $5,960M.
